phishing_attacks.definition: Phishing attacks trick people into sharing personal information like passwords or bank details by pretending to be trusted companies through fake emails, websites, or messages.
phishing_attacks.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66D (Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource)
phishing_attacks.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹1,00,000
safety_tips: Always verify sender's identity before clicking any links
Check website URLs carefully for spelling mistakes
Never share passwords or OTPs via email or phone
Use two-factor authentication on all accounts

malware_attacks.definition: Malware attacks use harmful software like viruses, trojans, or ransomware to damage computers, steal data, or gain unauthorized access to systems.
malware_attacks.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66 (Computer related offences) and Section 43 (Penalty for damage to computer, computer system, etc.)
malware_attacks.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹5,00,000
safety_tips: Install trusted antivirus software and keep it updated
Avoid downloading files from unknown sources
Don't click on suspicious links or pop-ups
Keep your operating system and software updated

denial_of_service.definition: DoS/DDoS attacks flood websites or servers with fake traffic to make them unavailable to real users, causing service disruption.
denial_of_service.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹5,00,000
safety_tips: Use DDoS protection services for websites
Monitor network traffic for unusual patterns
Keep server software updated and secure
Have backup servers ready for emergencies

hacking.definition: Hacking involves gaining unauthorized access to computer systems, networks, or accounts without permission to steal data or cause damage.
hacking.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66 (Computer related offences) and Section 43 (Penalty for damage to computer system)
hacking.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹5,00,000
safety_tips: Use strong, unique passwords for all accounts
Enable two-factor authentication everywhere
Keep software and systems updated
Monitor accounts for suspicious activity

identity_theft.definition: Identity theft involves stealing personal information like Aadhaar, PAN, or bank details to impersonate someone and commit fraud in their name.
identity_theft.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66C (Punishment for identity theft) and Section 66D (Punishment for cheating by personation)
identity_theft.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹1,00,000
safety_tips: Never share personal documents unnecessarily
Monitor bank statements regularly for suspicious activity
Use strong passwords and enable account alerts
Be careful about sharing personal information online

data_breach.definition: Data breach occurs when unauthorized persons access, steal, or expose sensitive information like personal data, passwords, or financial records from organizations.
data_breach.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 43A (Compensation for failure to protect data) and Section 72A (Punishment for disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract)
data_breach.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹5,00,000, plus compensation
safety_tips: Use different passwords for different accounts
Enable notifications for account activities
Regularly check if your data was breached online
Update passwords immediately if breach is reported

website_defacement.definition: Website defacement involves unauthorized modification of a website's appearance or content, often to display political messages or demonstrate hacking skills.
website_defacement.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66 (Computer related offences) and Section 43 (Penalty for damage to computer system)
website_defacement.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹5,00,000
safety_tips: Keep website software and plugins updated
Use strong admin passwords and two-factor authentication
Regular website backups to restore quickly
Monitor website for unauthorized changes

cyberstalking_cyberbullying.definition: Cyberstalking and cyberbullying involve using digital platforms to harass, threaten, or intimidate individuals repeatedly through messages, posts, or other online activities.
cyberstalking_cyberbullying.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66A (Punishment for sending offensive messages) and Section 67 (Punishment for publishing obscene material)
cyberstalking_cyberbullying.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine
safety_tips: Block and report abusive users immediately
Don't respond to or engage with cyberbullies
Save evidence of harassment for reporting
Adjust privacy settings on social media accounts

piracy_digital_content_theft.definition: Piracy and digital content theft involve unauthorized copying, distribution, or use of copyrighted material like movies, music, software, or books without permission.
piracy_digital_content_theft.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66 (Computer related offences) and Copyright Act 1957
piracy_digital_content_theft.penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹3,00,000
safety_tips: Use only licensed software and legal streaming services
Avoid downloading content from suspicious websites
Purchase original software and media content
Report piracy websites to authorities

financial_fraud.definition: Financial fraud includes UPI scams, fake banking websites, fraudulent transactions, and tricks to steal money through digital payment methods or online banking.
financial_fraud.indian_cyber_law: IT Act 2000 - Section 66D (Cheating by personation) and IPC Section 420 (Cheating)
financial_fraud.penalty: Imprisonment up to 7 years and/or fine
safety_tips: Never share OTP, PIN, or CVV with anyone
Verify payment requests before sending money
Use official banking apps and websites only
Enable transaction alerts and check statements regularly
